summary: Iter21 — SafeTradie Phase 2 Document Library Hub fully validated end-to-end across 8 doc types. Backend pytest 43/43 PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_iter21_doc_library.py (~13s): /api/docs/types returns exactly 6 categories + 8 types + 8 states with field schemas; auth enforced (401/403) on POST/GET-list/GET-single/PATCH/DELETE/PDF; unknown doc_type -> 404; per-type create returns doc_id (doc_<10hex>) + reference (PREFIX-YYYY-####) + status=draft + version=1; list filters by doc_type and excludes _id; GET single OK; PATCH persists status + arbitrary fields and verified via re-GET; PDF returns application/pdf with %PDF magic and >1000 bytes for ALL 8 types (jsa, risk_assessment, sssp, emergency_plan, hazardous_chemicals, site_induction, confined_space_permit, toolbox_talk_record); soft-delete archives then second DELETE hard-removes (404 thereafter). SWMS Phase 1 regression: list + create with full payload pass. Frontend verified live on owner@safetradie.demo against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL: /dashboard/document-library renders doc-library-hub with all 6 cat-tile-{safety,worker,contractor,incident,plant,trade} and all 8 cat-type-* cards + quick-type-select. Click cat-type-jsa -> /dashboard/document-library/jsa shows doc-list-page with doc-list-new + doc-list-search. Click New -> doc-form with doc-legal-notice + dynamic fields rendered from registry. Filling field-task + field-site, doc-save then doc-finish redirected back to list with the new row visible. doc-list-search filters correctly. Row-level pdf-{doc_id} button triggered an actual PDF download (17906 bytes, filename=JSA-2026-0004.pdf). Risk Assessment new flow also created (RA-2026-0003). SWMS Library page (/dashboard/swms) loads, plus regression checks on /dashboard/risk-register, /dashboard/incidents, /dashboard/automations all loaded with no .error elements. Note: actual frontend route is /dashboard/document-library/* (review_request mistakenly said /dashboard/documents/*) and backend list endpoint is GET /api/docs?doc_type=X (review_request mistakenly said GET /api/docs/{doc_type}); update method is PATCH not PUT and operates on doc_id not doc_type+doc_id. Tests were aligned to actual implementation and ALL functional behavior is correct per the schema-registry pattern.

design_issues.screen: /dashboard/document-library/:doc_type/new (Risk Assessment Review Date, JSA work_date, etc.)
issues: Date and datetime fields use native browser <input type='date'>/<input type='datetime-local'> in DocumentForm.jsx (FieldRenderer 'date'/'datetime' branches) — same inconsistency previously called out for SWMS step 1. Consider replacing with shadcn Calendar + Popover for visual consistency with the rest of the app.

action_items: (Doc accuracy) Update PRD/spec — actual routes are: list = GET /api/docs?doc_type=X (NOT GET /api/docs/{doc_type}); update = PATCH /api/docs/{doc_id} (NOT PUT /api/docs/{doc_type}/{doc_id}); delete/PDF/get-single also use /docs/{doc_id} only. Frontend route prefix is /dashboard/document-library/* (NOT /dashboard/documents/*). Either align review-request/PRD to code or refactor routes to match the spec.
(Nice-to-have) Replace native date / datetime-local inputs in DocumentForm FieldRenderer with shadcn Calendar component for UI consistency.
(Optional) Wrap WeasyPrint write_pdf in asyncio.wait_for(timeout=30) inside docs_module.get_pdf — same hardening recommended for SWMS PDF in iter20.
critical_code_review_comments: docs_module.py is 735 lines — within guideline but trending high. Consider splitting renderers (render_jsa..render_toolbox_record + _common_css/_render_common) into docs_pdf.py and route handlers into docs_routes.py; the registry stays in docs_module.py.

create_doc and update_doc accept arbitrary dict body with no Pydantic validation — clients can write unknown keys and accidentally shadow internal fields. The reserved-key pop in PATCH (doc_id, user_id, reference, created_at, doc_type, category) is good but POST does not pop these (relies on **{k:v for k,v in body.items() if k not in (...)} which DOES strip them). Suggest a DocCreate / DocUpdate Pydantic model per type or at least a generic DocPatch BaseModel.

PATCH /docs/{doc_id} does NOT bump version — review_request explicitly states 'PUT updates status/fields and bumps version'. Currently only updated_at changes. If versioning is intended for compliance audit, increment version on every successful $set (or on status transition).
delete_doc returns 200 with {archived:true} or {deleted:true} — REST-pure callers may expect 204 for delete. Minor.

ai_draft endpoint exists but is not in the review_request scope; nonetheless it spreads AI-returned dict over the entire doc via setForm({...f, ...r.data}) on the frontend which could overwrite reference/status/etc. Either filter the AI response to known field keys or strip reserved keys server-side before returning.

DocumentLibraryHub fetches /docs (no doc_type filter) and uses the result for both 'recent' and per-category counts — for users with hundreds of docs this loads up to 500 rows on the hub. Consider a /docs/stats aggregation endpoint returning {category: count} + recent (limit 5).
